senses.gloss:
mukhaliṅga
(‘liṅga with face’)
------------------------------------------
Śiva is worshipped in the form of a लिङ्ग. (See ŚIVALIṄGA for details.)
A लिङ्ग may be aniconic (without any image form) or partially iconic. The मुखलिङ्ग belongs to this latter group.
In a मुखलिङ्ग, the शिव-part is one unit more than the ब्रह्मा-part and the विष्णु-part.
If the शिव-part is divided into three equal portions, the mukha or face of शिव should occupy one and a half portion.
There may be one, two, three or four faces on the round shaft of the लिङ्ग. Whereas liṅgas with one face and four faces can be installed in villages and towns (i.e., human settlements), the two-faced ones are generally used in black-magical rites and are established in forests or on mountains.
The one-faced लिङ्ग must have the face turned towards the entrance of the sanctum.
If it is three faced, the main face should be turned towards the door of the sanctum.
